title: enrich._extract_tags keyword-matches connector boilerplate, polluting tag filters
description:
`backend/etl/enrich.py:218` `_extract_tags` builds tags by substring-matching `TAG_KEYWORDS` against `title + description`. Because connectors write templated boilerplate into those fields, every record from a large connector inherits the same tags.

Effect on the current database -- share of each tag that comes from HRSA FQHC records:

| tag | total tagged | from HRSA | % |
|---|---|---|---|
| employment | 18,793 | 17,929 | 95.4% |
| training | 5,008 | 4,752 | 94.9% |
| family | 3,276 | 2,979 | 90.9% |
| veteran | 20,120 | 18,303 | 91.0% |
| healthcare | 18,561 | 18,303 | 98.6% |

`backend/app/services/resource.py:186` filters on `tags` OR `subcategories`, so a tag filter for employment returns overwhelmingly health clinics.

Note `employment` and `training` are not in `TAG_KEYWORDS` and not emitted by `hrsa_health_centers._build_tags` -- so a third path is adding them (a backfill script or another enrich pass). Trace that before fixing, since the fix depends on which stage is responsible.

## Fix direction
- Do not derive tags from templated connector text -- match against fields the connector populates from real upstream data, or maintain a boilerplate blocklist
- Require a keyword to be more than an incidental substring match (word-boundary matching at minimum)
- Consider making derived tags opt-in per connector rather than global
acceptance_criteria:
- A tag filter returns resources genuinely about that tag
- No single connector accounts for >90% of any tag
- The origin of the employment/training tags on HRSA records is identified and closed off

title: Revive housing connectors: ssvf, hud_vash, gpd yield 1-2 resources each
description:
Housing is 964 resources (4.6% of DB), and the three Tier-1 VA housing programs contribute almost none of it:

| Source | Resources |
|---|---|
| SSVF FY26 Grantee Data | 2 |
| HUD-VASH Voucher Awards (2020-2024) | 1 |
| VA GPD FY24 Grantee Data | 1 |
| VA SSVF Program Directory | 0 |

Each of these upstream datasets has hundreds of grantees (SSVF and GPD grantee lists, HUD-VASH PHA awards). Producing 1-2 resources means the parse is succeeding on a header row or first record and then failing or filtering everything else out.

Note there are two SSVF sources registered (`SSVF FY26 Grantee Data` and `VA SSVF Program Directory`) -- consolidate to one.

Files: `backend/connectors/{ssvf,hud_vash,gpd}.py`, plus `backend/scripts/fetch_hud_vash_awards.py` and `fetch_hud_vash_multiyear.py`.

Housing is the highest-stakes category for the Veterans this site serves; 964 nationwide with 55 in California is thin.
acceptance_criteria:
- SSVF, HUD-VASH, and GPD each produce resource counts matching their published grantee/award lists
- Duplicate SSVF source rows consolidated
- Housing category coverage materially increases in every state

title: Revive employment/training connectors: careeronestop, apprenticeship, skillbridge, gi_bill_schools
description:
Employment is 854 resources (4.1% of DB) and training is 259 (1.2%). A Veteran searching employment in California gets 16 results. The connectors meant to fill this are all dark.

| Connector | Source row | Resources |
|---|---|---|
| `careeronestop` | none | -- |
| `apprenticeship` | none | -- |
| `gi_bill_schools` | none | -- |
| `skillbridge` | DOD SkillBridge Partner Directory | 1 |
| `veteran_employers` | Veteran Employers (Compiled) | 66 |
| `vboc` | SBA Veterans Business Outreach Centers | 29 |

Three never registered a source row at all; SkillBridge registered one and produced a single resource, which means the fetch or parse is failing after the first record.

## Highest-leverage
SkillBridge publishes a large partner directory (thousands of organizations) -- it is the single biggest available win for employment/training depth. `gi_bill_schools` (VA GIDS API) is similarly large for education.

## Checks
- CareerOneStop needs an API key + userId; confirm both are set in Railway env
- `backend/connectors/skillbridge.py` -- verify pagination and that the upstream file/endpoint still exists
- Run each with `dry_run=true` and inspect `result.stats.extracted` before committing

Files: `backend/connectors/{careeronestop,apprenticeship,skillbridge,gi_bill_schools}.py`
acceptance_criteria:
- All four connectors register source rows and complete runs
- employment + training categories grow substantially beyond the current 1,113 combined
- Per-state employment coverage is no longer in the single/low-double digits for large states

title: Revive VA facilities connectors: va_gov and vet_centers yield zero resources
description:
The VA Lighthouse-backed connectors are the backbone of the directory and currently contribute nothing.

- `VA.gov` source row exists with 0 resources and a NULL `last_run` -- it has never successfully run.
- `vet_centers` has no source row at all, meaning `VetCentersConnector` has never completed a run that registered a source.

Both are registered in `backend/jobs/refresh.py` CONNECTOR_REGISTRY. Files: `backend/connectors/va_gov.py`, `backend/connectors/vet_centers.py`.

## Likely causes to check first
- Lighthouse API key missing/expired in Railway env (the connectors need a VA API key)
- Lighthouse API endpoint or response schema changed since the connector was written
- The ETL run never being triggered for these connector names

## Why this matters
VA facilities and Vet Centers are Tier 1 and Veteran-specific. Restoring them adds genuine healthcare and mentalHealth resources that displace HRSA's general-population FQHC rows in relevance ranking, and gives the "beyond VA.gov" comparison a real baseline.

Start with a dry run:
```
POST /api/v1/admin/jobs/refresh/run?connector_name=va_gov&dry_run=true
```
acceptance_criteria:
- Both connectors complete a run and register source rows
- Resource counts are in the expected order of magnitude (VA health facilities and ~300 Vet Centers)
- Failures surface as non-HEALTHY rather than silent zero

title: Source health reports HEALTHY for 27 sources that yield zero resources
description:
27 of 58 sources have `health_status = HEALTHY` and `error_count = 0` while producing 0 resources. The dashboard is reporting false green, which is why the collection gap went unnoticed and healthcare grew to 88.9% of the DB.

Zero-resource sources still marked HEALTHY include: VA.gov, Department of Labor - VETS, Wounded Warrior Project, VA SSVF Program Directory, National Veterans Legal Services Program, The American Legion, DAV, Tunnel to Towers Veterans Villages, Texas Veterans Commission, Home Base, Give an Hour, Swords to Plowshares, Veteran Certification Programs, AI Discovery, Vibe4Vets Hub Data.

Near-zero but also HEALTHY: HUD-VASH Voucher Awards (1), VA GPD FY24 (1), DOD SkillBridge (1), SSVF FY26 (2), VA Stand Down Events (3).

Several of these have a `last_run` timestamp (2026-01-29 / 2026-02-20), so the job ran and returned nothing without flagging it.

## Fix
In `backend/app/services/health.py`, treat a completed run that produced zero resources as DEGRADED (or FAILED after N consecutive zero-yield runs) rather than HEALTHY. A connector that silently returns an empty list is the failure mode that actually happens here -- exceptions are already handled.

Also worth surfacing: sources whose yield drops sharply run-over-run.

## Verify
```sql
SELECT s.name, s.health_status, s.last_run::date, s.error_count, count(DISTINCT r.id) AS res
FROM sources s LEFT JOIN source_records sr ON sr.source_id=s.id
LEFT JOIN resources r ON r.id=sr.resource_id AND r.status!='INACTIVE'
GROUP BY 1,2,3,4 HAVING count(DISTINCT r.id) < 5 ORDER BY 5 DESC, 1;
```
acceptance_criteria:
- A connector run yielding 0 resources sets a non-HEALTHY status
- The admin dashboard distinguishes "ran and found nothing" from "ran successfully"
- Backfilling current state flags all 27 zero-yield sources

title: Rebalance resource distribution: healthcare is 88.9% of the database
description:
Analysis of the 2026-07-10 production backup (21,211 active resources) found the directory is overwhelmingly one general-population health dataset, while the Veteran-specific Tier-1 backbone produces almost nothing.

## Category distribution
| category | n | % of DB |
|---|---|---|
| healthcare | 18,587 | 88.9% |
| housing | 964 | 4.6% |
| employment | 854 | 4.1% |
| legal | 661 | 3.2% |
| food | 598 | 2.9% |
| benefits | 548 | 2.6% |
| mentalHealth | 299 | 1.4% |
| supportServices | 270 | 1.3% |
| training | 259 | 1.2% |
| education | 191 | 0.9% |
| family | 147 | 0.7% |
| financial | 144 | 0.7% |

## Root cause
18,303 of the 18,587 healthcare resources (98.5%) come from one connector, `backend/connectors/hrsa_health_centers.py`, which hardcodes `categories=["healthcare"]` (line 186) for every row of the HRSA FQHC service-delivery CSV. That single connector is 86% of the entire database.

## Why California looks extreme
HRSA is a general-population dataset, so state counts track clinic infrastructure, not Veteran need: CA 2,901 / NY 844 / TX 819 / FL 771 / NC 753 / KY 663 / WV 508. TX and FL have Veteran populations comparable to CA's but roughly a quarter the FQHC sites.

## Framing
Healthcare is not over-collected -- everything else is barely collected. 27 sources report HEALTHY with zero resources (including VA.gov and DOL VETS), and vet_centers / careeronestop / gi_bill_schools / apprenticeship never registered a source row at all.

Sequence: fix collection (Track 1), then scope HRSA correctly (Track 2), then clean up the classification pollution it caused (Track 3).

## Reproducing the analysis
Restore a prod backup into a scratch container:
```
docker run -d --name v4v-analysis -e POSTGRES_PASSWORD=analysis -e POSTGRES_USER=v4v -e POSTGRES_DB=v4v postgres:17
zcat backups/vibe4vets_YYYYMMDD_HHMMSS.sql.gz | docker exec -i v4v-analysis psql -U v4v -d v4v
```
Note: do not bind a host port on WSL2 (Docker Desktop port-forwarding fails); use `docker exec` instead.
acceptance_criteria:
- Healthcare is under ~40% of active resources
- No single connector exceeds ~25% of the database
- Every registered source either yields resources or reports a non-HEALTHY status

title: Backfill: strip incorrect employment/training/family tags from HRSA resources
description:
One-time cleanup of tags already written to production by the enrich bug. Must land after the `_extract_tags` fix, otherwise the next connector run re-pollutes.

Affected: 17,929 HRSA resources tagged `employment`, 4,752 tagged `training`, 2,979 tagged `family`, 515 tagged `housing`.

Remove tags that do not describe the resource, keeping the legitimately descriptive ones (`fqhc`, `community-health-center`, `primary-care`, `sliding-fee-scale`, `affordable-healthcare`, `federally-qualified`, `permanent-site`, `mobile-clinic`, `school-based`, `dental`).

Follow the pattern in the existing one-off scripts under `backend/scripts/` (e.g. `fix_feeding_america_categories.py`). Run against a restored backup first and diff the tag frequency table before and after.
acceptance_criteria:
- HRSA resources carry only tags that describe them
- Tag frequency table shows no single connector dominating employment/training/family
- Script is idempotent and safe to re-run

title: Scope HRSA FQHCs: keep VA-gap sites as resources, move the rest to a nearby-only lookup
description:
`hrsa_health_centers.py` contributes 18,303 resources -- 86% of the database and 98.5% of the healthcare category. These are general-population FQHC sites, not Veteran resources: every record carries identical boilerplate eligibility ("Open to all patients, including Veterans, regardless of insurance status..."), all 18,303 have empty `subcategories`, and records include things like `CHOICES Domestic Violence Shelter` filed under healthcare.

Do not delete the data -- FQHCs are genuinely useful for Veterans with other-than-honorable discharges or no VA enrollment, which is squarely the "beyond VA.gov" value proposition. The problem is that 18k undifferentiated clinics dominate browse, counts, and search ranking.

## Proposed approach
Keep as first-class resources only the FQHC sites that fill a VA gap:
- location_setting of homeless-services, public-housing, or migrant-health (already derivable -- the connector tags these at `_build_tags`)
- plus any site beyond ~40 miles of the nearest VA facility (needs the VA facilities connector working first -- see the va_gov/vet_centers issue)

Move the remainder behind the `/api/v1/resources/nearby` healthcare lookup so they surface on location search but do not appear in category browse or drive category counts.

Expected: ~18,000 down to roughly 2,000-3,000 first-class resources, keeping the highest-signal ones.

## Open decision
Whether "demoted" means a `status`/visibility flag on Resource, a separate table, or a `scope`-like discriminator. Worth deciding before implementing, since search, counts, and the nearby endpoint all need to respect it consistently.

Sequence after the Track 1 connector work -- the ratio may look very different once the Veteran-specific sources are producing.
acceptance_criteria:
- Healthcare no longer dominates category counts
- FQHCs still reachable via nearby/location search
- The VA-gap subset is retained as browsable resources with real subcategories

title: Audit the remaining zero-yield sources and retire or fix each
description:
After the VA facilities, employment, and housing connectors are addressed, work through the rest of the zero-yield sources. Each should end up either producing resources or being retired so the source list reflects reality.

Zero resources, never ran (NULL `last_run`): Department of Labor - VETS, National Veterans Legal Services Program, The American Legion, DAV (Disabled American Veterans), Texas Veterans Commission, VA SSVF Program Directory, AI Discovery, AI Discovery - Benefits (Multi-Region), DMV Benefits Consultation Data, National Food Assistance Collection, Vibe4Vets Hub Data.

Zero resources, ran and found nothing (`last_run` 2026-01-29/30): Wounded Warrior Project, Home Base, Give an Hour, Swords to Plowshares, Tunnel to Towers Veterans Villages, Veteran Certification Programs.

Very low yield worth a look: VA Stand Down Events (3), Cohen Veterans Network (1), Boulder Crest Foundation (1), Final Salute Inc. (1), The Headstrong Project (1), VFW Post Locator (6), DAV Chapters (8), Military OneSource (7).

Some of these are legitimately small (a single organization with one program). The point is to make that explicit rather than leaving it ambiguous against genuine failures.

Depends on the health-status fix so the audit has a reliable signal to work from.
acceptance_criteria:
- Every source is either producing resources, marked as intentionally small, or removed
- No source remains HEALTHY with zero resources and a NULL last_run

title: Add healthcare subcategories so the healthcare tag filter does something
description:
All 18,303 HRSA resources have an empty `subcategories` array, so the largest category in the database has zero filtering granularity. `/api/v1/taxonomy/tags/healthcare` has nothing meaningful to offer.

Per CLAUDE.md, frontend tag filters must match actual values in `subcategories` and `tags`, with `ELIGIBILITY_TAGS` in `backend/app/core/taxonomy.py` as the source of truth.

Add healthcare subcategories (hyphenated, per the existing convention) covering at least: `primary-care`, `dental`, `behavioral-health`, `mobile-clinic`, `school-based`, `telehealth`, `vet-center`, `va-medical-center`.

Populate them from data the HRSA connector already has -- `_build_tags` derives location type and setting, and `raw_data` retains the upstream fields. Also apply to the VA facilities connectors once those are producing.

Verify with:
```
curl "http://localhost:8000/api/v1/resources?categories=healthcare&tags=dental"
```
acceptance_criteria:
- Healthcare resources carry meaningful subcategories
- taxonomy.py ELIGIBILITY_TAGS includes the new values
- Filtering healthcare by subcategory returns correct, non-empty results
